newsitem.title: USA: Balloonist changes route, ending bid for record.
newsitem.headline: Balloonist changes route, ending bid for record.

text.p: American Steve Fossett, denied permission to pass over Libya, changed his route Friday on a course that will likely end his bid to become the first to circle the globe nonstop in a balloon, his expedition said.

"The team and Steve are very disappointed," project manager Bo Kemper told reporters. "But on the other hand it has been an unbelievably successful trip. Equipment worked 100 percent. The weather was working 100 percent. The only thing that didn't work was political."

Kemper refused to say all hope was lost, but told reporters that Fossett's new route over Niger and Chad and then Egypt would use up so much fuel that the "Solo Spirit" balloon would probably have to put down in India.
Fossett's consolation prize, he said, will probably be a new record for time spent in a balloon. The current mark is six days and 16 minutes. He began the voyage late Monday night in St. Louis.
Kemper said the expedition had gone through numerous channels trying to win permission from Libya, but got the denial in a message signed off "best regards" while Fossett was drifting over Algeria.
That happened just after Fossett broke his own record for balloon distance travel when he reached 5,435 miles (8,747 km) on a journey from South Korea to Canada.
